title: Searching Far and Long. I. Pilot ALMA 2 mm Follow-up of Bright Dusty Galaxies as a Redshift Filter
question: To identify the highest-z sources from a sample of bright 850 micron-selected DSFGs, provide an independent measurement of the volume density of z > 3 DSFGs, and test the practical utility of 2 mm follow up observations as a redshift filter.

data.sensitivity: median rms 0.08 mJy beam^-1 (range 0.07 - 0.11 mJy beam^-1)

what.value: S2CLS 850 um catalog, positions, and deboosted flux densities; UDS SCUBA-2 map

evidence.quote: To select our sample, we drew from the 850$\,\rm{\mu m}$-selected submillimeter galaxies (SMGs) observed with SCUBA-2 as part of the SCUBA-2 Cosmology Legacy Survey (cite: s2cls).

We adopt deboosted flux densities from S2CLS (cite: s2cls) to account for confusion and Eddington boosting, i.e. flux-limited sample bias wherein more sources have fluxes boosted rather than decreased by noise.

Given the overall rarity of $S_{850\rm\,\mu m} > 5.55$\,mJy sources among DSFGs, we estimate the impact of cosmic variance, and of incompleteness due to shallower S2CLS data of SSA22 relative to other fields like the UDS (cite: s2cls) and COSMOS (cite: 2019simpson) SCUBA-2 maps.

what.value: AzTEC 1.1 mm flux densities, AzTEC map, OIR and mm/radio photometric redshifts, and spectroscopic redshift of SSA.0001

evidence.quote: About a third of our targets (14/39) also have optical-infrared (OIR) photometric redshifts and about one quarter (9/39) have mm/radio photometric redshifts (beyond those we calculate herein), both reported in (cite: umehata2014).
We crossmatch our SSA22 sources with reported AzTEC 1.1\,mm flux densities from (cite: umehata2014) and find $\sim70\%$ (27/39) of our sample is detected down to SNR of 3.8.

what.value: Spectroscopic redshifts for SSA.0007, SSA.0009, and SSA.0019

evidence.quote: SSA.0007 is resolved into two components in our 2\,mm data and is also spectroscopically confirmed as part of a dense group within the protocluster at $z = 3.09$, possibly in a multiple merger phase (cite: 2015umehata; 2016kubo; 2017umehata; 2018umehata; 2019umehata).

In addition to the sources confirmed in the protocluster, three galaxies are confirmed spectroscopically to be in the foreground of the protocluster: SSA.0009 at $z = 2.555$ (cite: 2005chapman), SSA.0019 at $z = 2.278$ (cite: 2012alaghbandzadeh), and SSA.0031 at $z = 2.6814$ (confirmed via Lyman-$\alpha$ emission; Cooper et al. in prep).
We crossmatch our sample to the X-ray catalog for SSA22 presented in (cite: 2009lehmer) to check for the presence of luminous active galactic nuclei (AGN).

what.value: Herschel/SPIRE 250, 350, and 500 um deblended maps and catalogs using MIPS 24 um priors

evidence.quote: *Herschel*/SPIRE measurements of SSA22 at 250$\,\rm{\mu m}$, 350$\,\rm{\mu m}$, and 500$\,\rm{\mu m}$ were extracted using cross-matched positional priors from MIPS 24$\,\rm{\mu m}$ data (cite: swinbank2014; 2016kato).
As the data are confusion limited, we adopt the confusion error from (cite: spire) for any sources with derived errors less than these confusion error limits.

what.value: ALESS 870 um and 2 mm sample for redshift and beta comparison

evidence.quote: To compare to our sample, we take the subset of 25/99 ALESS sources with $S_{870\rm\,\mu m} \geq 5$\,mJy from (cite: 2021dacunha), and find a median redshift and 68% confidence interval of $z_{\rm med} = 3.2^{+0.4}_{-1.1}$.

recipe.goal: Measure 2 mm continuum flux densities and noise from ALMA images
recipe.method: Extract peak flux density and rms from primary-beam-corrected images within the SCUBA-2 beam (7.5 arcsec radius) using CASA imstat, adopting a 3 sigma detection threshold; sum components for resolved pair SSA.0007
key_parameters: search radius = 7.5 arcsec (SCUBA-2 beam); detection threshold = 3 sigma
assumptions: Detected sources are unresolved at 1.7'' x 1.4'' resolution (except SSA.0007 which is resolved into two physically associated components)

recipe.goal: Crossmatch and extract multiwavelength ancillary photometry and literature redshifts
recipe.method: Crossmatch ALMA 2 mm positions (or S2CLS positions for <3 sigma sources) to literature redshifts, X-ray catalog, AzTEC 1.1 mm catalog/map, and Herschel/SPIRE 250, 350, 500 um maps/catalogs; combine statistical and absolute calibration uncertainties in quadrature
key_parameters: Calibration uncertainties: 4% Herschel, 5% SCUBA-2, 10% AzTEC, 5% ALMA; MIPS 24 um FWHM = 7''
assumptions: Herschel/SPIRE measurements are confusion limited; deboosted S2CLS 850 um fluxes account for Eddington boosting

recipe.goal: Estimate millimeter photometric redshifts and bin sample by redshift
recipe.method: Fit FIR/mm photometry (250, 350, 500, 850, 1100, 2000 um) with MMpz to derive photo-z PDFs; integrate PDFs in delta_z = 0.1 intervals and use the 3 highest probability intervals to sort galaxies into low-z, mid-z (2.6 < z < 3.6), and high-z bins; also test mock SEDs with/without 2 mm
key_parameters: beta = 1.8 (fixed in MMpz); PDF integration width delta_z = 0.1; mid-z bin 2.6 < z < 3.6 centered on z = 3.1
assumptions: Empirical L_IR - lambda_peak relation with no redshift evolution of lambda_peak (and T_dust); fixed beta = 1.8

recipe.goal: Fit IR SEDs and derive physical properties (beta, L_IR, T_dust, lambda_peak, SFR, M_gas, depletion time)
recipe.method: Fix redshift to best available (spec-z, else OIR photo-z, else z_MMpz) and fit 6-band FIR/mm photometry to a modified blackbody added piecewise with a mid-IR power law using Bayesian MCMC; convert L_IR to SFR; derive M_gas from 2 mm continuum using Scoville et al. (2016) Eq. 16 and compute depletion time
key_parameters: Fixed parameters: alpha_MIR = 2, lambda_0 = 200 um; Free parameters: beta, L_IR (8-1000 um), T_dust, lambda_peak; mass-weighted T_dust = 25 K for M_gas
assumptions: General opacity model with tau = 1 at lambda_rest = 200 um; CMB heating correction included; Chabrier IMF; Planck cosmology (H_0 = 67.7 km s^-1 Mpc^-1, Omega_lambda = 0.6911); gravitational lensing by foreground protocluster is negligible

recipe.goal: Estimate CSFRD contribution, volume density, cosmic variance, and sample incompleteness
recipe.method: Run 100-trial Monte Carlo sampling redshift and SFR PDFs across 0.28 deg^2 SSA22 survey area in z bins of width 0.5 from 1 < z < 5; estimate incompleteness by MC trials placing 0.28 deg^2 areas in UDS and COSMOS SCUBA-2 maps with and without noise boosting; adjust CSFRD by incompleteness factor
key_parameters: 100 MC trials; SSA22 area = 0.28 deg^2; redshift bins 1 < z < 5 with width delta_z = 0.5; incompleteness factor = 1.6 (+0.6/-0.8)
assumptions: UDS and COSMOS S2CLS fields represent cosmic average density

answer_key.quantity: Number of ALMA 2 mm detected targets (>3 sigma)

evidence.quote: Out of the 39 targets, 35 targets were detected in the 2\,mm observations above this threshold.

answer_key.quantity: Net average positional offset between S2CLS and ALMA 2 mm (>3 sigma sources)

evidence.quote: Comparing S2CLS reported coordinates to our measured coordinates of sources with flux densities $> 3\sigma$, we find an average RA offset of $1.64\ensuremath{''}\pm0.92\ensuremath{''}$ and an average Dec offset of $-1.0\ensuremath{''}\pm 0.7\ensuremath{''}$, for a total net average offset of $1.9\ensuremath{''}\pm 1.2\ensuremath{''}$.
For the full sample, we find a median $\langle z \rangle = 2.7 \pm 0.2$.

answer_key.quantity: Median redshift of low-z bin (16 galaxies)

evidence.quote: From our millimeter photo-$z$ measurements and ancillary redshift information, we find 16 low-$z$ galaxies with median $\langle z_{\rm{low}-z} \rangle = 2.08 \pm 0.16$, 17 mid-$z$ galaxies with median $\langle z_{\rm{mid}-z} \rangle = 2.98 \pm 0.11$, and 6 high-$z$ galaxies with median $\langle z_{\rm{high}-z} \rangle = 3.8 \pm 0.3$, as shown in Figure [2](#fig:zbins).

answer_key.quantity: Median redshift of mid-z bin (17 galaxies)

evidence.quote: From our millimeter photo-$z$ measurements and ancillary redshift information, we find 16 low-$z$ galaxies with median $\langle z_{\rm{low}-z} \rangle = 2.08 \pm 0.16$, 17 mid-$z$ galaxies with median $\langle z_{\rm{mid}-z} \rangle = 2.98 \pm 0.11$, and 6 high-$z$ galaxies with median $\langle z_{\rm{high}-z} \rangle = 3.8 \pm 0.3$, as shown in Figure [2](#fig:zbins).

answer_key.quantity: Median redshift of high-z bin (6 galaxies)

evidence.quote: From our millimeter photo-$z$ measurements and ancillary redshift information, we find 16 low-$z$ galaxies with median $\langle z_{\rm{low}-z} \rangle = 2.08 \pm 0.16$, 17 mid-$z$ galaxies with median $\langle z_{\rm{mid}-z} \rangle = 2.98 \pm 0.11$, and 6 high-$z$ galaxies with median $\langle z_{\rm{high}-z} \rangle = 3.8 \pm 0.3$, as shown in Figure [2](#fig:zbins).

answer_key.quantity: Redshift accuracy Delta z/(1+z) with 2 mm data (from mock SEDs)

evidence.quote: Specifically, our models suggest the addition of 2\,mm to a moderately constrained IR SED will improve the accuracy of a millimeter-derived redshift from $\Delta z/(1+z) = 0.3$ to $\Delta z/(1+z) = 0.2$.

evidence.loc: Utility of 2 mm as a Redshift Filter
evidence.quote: From these simulated SEDs, the addition of the 2\,mm point – provided $\sim500$$\,\rm{\mu m}$\, constraints exist – improves accuracy from $\Delta z/(1+z) = 0.3$ (without the 2\,mm data) to $\Delta z/(1+z) = 0.2$ (with the 2\,mm data), in particular for galaxies at $z \gtrsim 3.5$.

As our targets are selected for being among the brightest 850$\,\rm{\mu m}$-selected DSFGs in the SCUBA-2 survey, we find generally high IR luminosities such that all may be categorized as ultraluminous IR galaxies (ULIRGs, $L_{\rm IR} \geq 10^{12}$\,L$_{\rm \odot}$), with a median of $\rm log\,L_{\rm IR} = 12.7 \pm 0.2$.
We find characteristically high SFRs $\sim 500 - 1000$ M$_{\rm \odot}$\,yr$^{-1}$, with median SFR = $700 \pm 400$ M$_{\rm \odot}$\,yr$^{-1}$.

Peak wavelength measurements span 70\,$\,\rm{\mu m}$$< \lambda_{\rm peak} < 149$\,$\,\rm{\mu m}$, and consequently dust temperatures span $27 \rm\, K < \rm T_{\rm dust} < 72$ K, with a median $\rm T_{\rm dust} = 45 \pm 8$\,K.

answer_key.quantity: Median dust emissivity spectral index (beta) for full sample

evidence.quote: Our IR SED characterizations provide evidence for relatively high emissivity spectral indices ($\langle \beta \rangle = 2.4\pm0.3$) in the sample.

Overall, the measured emissivity spectral index, $\beta$, is consistent (within uncertainties) for the three subsamples at $\beta \sim 2.4$, with a median of $\langle \beta \rangle = 2.4 \pm 0.3$ for the full sample.

We find gas depletion times around $\tau \sim 200$ Myr with median and standard deviation $\tau = 220 \pm 160$ Myr, consistent with the majority of $z \gtrsim 1$ DSFGs (cite: swinbank2014; 2020dudz; 2021sun).

answer_key.quantity: Contribution of S_850um > 5.55 mJy DSFGs to CSFRD (2 < z < 5)

evidence.quote: We measure that especially bright ($S_{850\rm\mu m}>5.55$\,mJy) DSFGs contribute $\sim10$% to the cosmic-averaged CSFRD from $2<z<5$, confirming findings from previous work with similar samples.
Our 850$\,\rm{\mu m}$-bright, obscured sources contribute $\sim10$% (ranging 8-13%) to the cosmic-averaged CSFRD from $2<z<5$.

answer_key.quantity: Volume density of S_850um > 5.55 mJy DSFGs at 4 < z < 5

evidence.quote: For a 100-trail MC, we find the volume density of DSFGs from $4 < z < 5$ to be $6.3\times10^{-7}\rm\,Mpc^{-3}$ based on our sample.

From this sampling of UDS/COSMOS maps, we determine that our SSA22 sample is not cosmologically over- or under-dense, but it is incomplete (in its representation of all $S_{850\rm\,\mu m}>5.55\,$mJy sources) by a factor of $1.6^{+0.6}_{-0.8}$.

score_reason: The ALMA 2 mm data reduction and peak flux measurement recipe (CASA 5.6.0, robust=2, PB correction, imstat within 7.5'' radius) is simple and fully reproducible, and Table 1 provides all 850 um and 2 mm fluxes. However, reproducing the full 6-band MMpz and Bayesian SED fits is blocked by the absence of a published table for the extracted Herschel/SPIRE and AzTEC fluxes (some extracted from privately shared maps) and reliance on an unpublished SED fitting code (Drew & Casey, submitted).
rediscovery_reason: The ALMA project 2019.1.00313.S is public, the 39 continuum pointings are small and fast to image, and all 39 ALMA 2 mm flux densities, uncertainties, and astrometric offsets are explicitly tabulated in Table 1 for direct numerical verification.
